Ubisoft lays off 166 in Canada across Montréal and Quebec City
The cuts come from the Montréal and Quebec City offices, two studios that have historically benefited from sizable subsidies offered by the Canadian government to bolster the country's game development industry.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
November 19, 2026
schedule
1 Min Read
expand_content
Image via Ubisoft
Ubisoft has confirmed that the company has cut 166 jobs in Montréal and Quebec City today, attributing the layoffs to ever-changing production needs.
The 166 positions come mostly from production and support roles,
according to GamesIndustry.biz
. Some proportion of that number is made up of employees from Vantage Studio, Ubisoft's joint-venture with Tencent that oversees Assassin's Creed, Far Cry, and Rainbow Six—the company's biggest moneymaking franchises.
The collaborative division was founded in 2025
, uniting studios from Montréal, Quebec, Sherbrooke, Saguenay, Barcelona, and Sofia to focus on a few properties.
Gamesindustry.biz reports that the layoffs were due to cancelled projects or ones that had been significantly rescoped, but there is no word from Ubisoft of what those projects might be.
"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognize the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources," Ubisoft said in a statement.
Related:
Take-Two lays off Firaxis employees on eve of Grand Theft Auto VI launch
These layoffs come months after Ubisoft shuttered its Halifax studio which also, like today's studios,
saw massive tax breaks and subsidies
through local employment-boosting programs in Canada. Today's layoffs are a hard hit to studios that make up a foundational part of the region's game development scene.
